title: Volume 2 Chapter 4: To You Whose Voice Cannot Reach Me, and to You Whom I Can Touch 1
content: “Darling, that’s just impossible.”
Merseja sighed as she said this while sitting across the table.
“What’s this Rainibati No. 5?
That’s not something that should just be out in the world.
Trying to use that to assassinate someone is a first in history.
I thought it was a gem meant for a quiet hermit life, but to be making a name for themselves in less than two months since being exiled is just too much, I think.”
Knowing about Rainibati No. 5, I was impressed that she was indeed an adventurer hired by the Chancellor.
That said, her sharp reasoning was quite something.
“And what’s all this commotion about?”
Merseja looked around as she spoke.
By the way, it was now two days after returning from the Demon Realm, and we were at a table set up on the main street of Hekatai in a temporary dining area for adventurers.
Merseja had arrived in town yesterday for a regular report, and today we were updating each other on recent events.
And the atmosphere around us could only be described as festive.
Drunken citizens and adventurers were singing and dancing everywhere.
“Somehow, when we returned to Hekatai, the news that we went to the Demon Realm to retrieve a sacred artifact had spread throughout the town.”
“…So, because you all safely brought back the sacred artifact, we have this festival?”
Yes, that was it.
For some reason, the rumor that we had gone to retrieve the sacred artifact had spread throughout the town.
Moreover, since the source of the rumor was the Church, or rather the Bishop, it was treated more as a fact than a rumor.
Once we returned the artifact to the Bishop, it was announced publicly, and I couldn’t make sense of it.
Didn’t they want to keep it discreet?
Is it really okay for the Church? This is a major scandal.
“Well, once the Church announced it, there’s nothing we can do about it.”
I nodded at Merseja, who said this while sipping her tea, agreeing that it wasn’t my fault.
At that moment, Merseja leaned in closer and whispered.
“So?
According to what you said, Shara the Sister is innocent, but the Church… the Bishop can’t be innocent, can he?
After all, aside from that Sister, the only one who knows about your actions that day is probably the Bishop.
Isn’t the public announcement an attempt to obscure that?”
I shrugged in response to Merseja’s question.
“I thought the same thing. While I was at it, I decided to probe Shara.”
On the way back from the Demon Realm, I explained our situation to Shara.
In other words, Erika was Erika Solnzali, falsely accused of assassinating the Light Priestess and exiled from the country.
And she was being targeted for her life by someone.
To put it simply, Shara was very angry.
Was the Church in Faltarl full of fools?
I thought that if she was angry, maybe she’d let something slip if I probed her.
When I mentioned that she still had doubts about the Bishop, she got just as angry at the Church of Faltarl.
“According to Shara, this request to retrieve the sacred artifact was apparently already communicated to the lord by that night after we were requested.”
Since I hadn’t lowered my voice particularly, Merseja straightened up.
“And the next day, it seems a request for cooperation was sent to the Adventurer Guild through the lord.”
“What’s with that? What a nonsensical move by the Bishop.”
Merseja exclaimed in disbelief.
“Even though he said it’d be bad if it got out, it seems the Bishop thought he wanted to cooperate just enough to not draw too much attention, given the difficulty of the request.”
In other words, by going through the lord, who had strong ties with the Adventurer Guild, he tried to use reliable adventurers to support us.
The Bishop probably didn’t expect that Erika would set out for the Demon Realm with only a day’s preparation, so we didn’t receive any support.
Also, to add, the Bishop was overly trusting of people’s discretion.
“So, what you’re saying is that by the same day the request was made, the lord knew about it, and by the next day, those who knew about it through the Adventurer Guild were already aware?”
When I nodded in response, Merseja sighed and shook her head.
In other words, the number of people who knew about our actions was far greater than I had imagined.
Considering how the rumor had spread, it was ridiculous to even count.
Naturally, it was difficult to narrow down who the assassin was or who leaked information to those plotting the assassination.
“And now that Rainibati No. 5 has come into play, it’s unlikely that the Church is trying to assassinate anyone.”

If the Church had obtained something like Rainibati No. 5, or had the means to acquire it, it would cause a commotion far beyond the mere fact that a part of the sacred artifact was left in the Demon Realm’s forest.
It could lead to a war between countries and the Church across the continent.
“Well, that’s probably true.
Even if we set aside the fact that they turn people into demons, the combination of the Church and Rainibati is just too far-fetched.”
Merseja looked as if she wanted to say “Good grief.”
“So? Have you found out anything on your end?”
An adventurer walking down the street noticed me and raised his bottle of alcohol in a toast, and I responded casually while asking Merseja.
“No, nothing in Faltarl. I consulted with the Chancellor, but…”
“What did he say?”
“He was trying to mobilize the Marquis’ knight order upon learning that an assassin was targeting you.”
I could easily imagine the Chancellor’s face turning bright red.
Well, he was stopped by everyone in the household and had to give up, Merseja said with a faraway look.
“By the way, why have the adventurers passing by been asking for handshakes, toasting, and offering drinks to you?”
While downing what I thought was my fifth or maybe sixth glass of Adventure Alcohol, I replied.
“Just imagine for a moment.”
A massive horde of monsters spilling out of the Demon Realm’s forest, the adventurers who had entered the forest retreating in a panic.
The adventurers in the Demon Realm must have thought this.
This is bad; this might be a repeat of sixty years ago.
They sent an inexperienced adventurer to the town as a messenger, and the adventurers present quickly formed a defensive line.
The adventurers must have felt a sense of dread.
After all, it was the beginning of a battle whose end was uncertain.
The whims of the Demon Realm were constant, but even so, it was unusual for such a large number of monsters to spill out from the forest.
The hastily assembled joint defense held, however.
By the time reinforcements were hastily gathered from the town, a massive explosion occurred in the Demon Realm’s forest.
The makeshift battle line and command structure were on the verge of collapse, but they managed to pull through.
The horde of monsters actually began to retreat.
They seized the opportunity to push the line forward; what was that explosion? That was something to think about later.
The adventurers had succeeded; the monsters were finally fleeing back to the forest.
Victory cries erupted, and the excitement among the adventurers reached its peak.
Then, two adventurers and a Sister emerged, cutting through the horde of monsters.
Suddenly, someone mentioned a rumor they heard in town, that there were adventurers who received a secret request from the Bishop.
Apparently, they were supposed to retrieve a sacred artifact left behind in the Demon Realm’s forest.

Then they started coming out, saying they heard about a pair of adventurers from Faltarl, and that the man was a disciple of that “Kind Barbara,” who set out for the Demon Realm’s forest today to retrieve it as soon as possible.
In the midst of all this, a story began to form among the adventurers.
The forest of the Demon Realm bared its fangs at the adventurers who came to retrieve the sacred artifact.

Undeterred, the adventurers pressed deeper into the forest, found the artifact, and with some mysterious power of the artifact, they cleared a path through the forest, causing the monsters to retreat in fear.
In other words, it was another adventurer who had pulled off a feat similar to ours.
“What’s with that ridiculous vibe?”
Merseja said, looking as if she had a headache.
Honestly, I didn’t quite get it either.
But according to Shara, this was how it was among the adventurers in Hekatai.
Adventurers were mostly people who had no other options, deciding to make a living through violence at the risk of their lives.
In other words, they were generally not very bright.
With a believable story circulating, and with the Bishop making a grand announcement about the retrieval of the sacred artifact, we were now treated as heroes among the adventurers in Hekatai.
It was probably a vibe of “Our fellow adventurers accomplished a great feat, yay!”
It was quite different from the vibe among adventurers in Faltarl, so I was at a loss as to how to respond.
Merseja sighed deeply and said,
“I thought you were going to try to live quietly, darling.”
“I did think that.”
“You did?”
“I realized it was unrealistic for Erika Solnzali to live quietly.”
Merseja glared at me with half-open eyes as I shrugged.
“You should have realized that before doing something that got you treated as a hero in less than two months, darling.”
I averted my gaze from Merseja’s words and waved at Erika and Shara, who were walking toward us.

In Hekatai, Barrel, an adventurer who thought he could live a decent life with a decent income, was running around the hastily assembled defensive line, thinking he had seen at least twenty people die.
He hadn’t been counting for a while and didn’t remember much, but he vividly remembered the first time.
It was probably because he felt he had done something out of character.
It was a boy with reddish-brown hair.
Although he was about the same age as that Longdagger, he was completely out of place in this situation.
Even without being a master, it was clear that the boy’s skills were lacking.
He was obviously a boy who was insufficiently skilled.
What was this kid’s master teaching him? Barrel wondered with a boiled head, unable to take a proper break.
Adventurers lived in a world of self-responsibility. Therefore, they taught their disciples to discern.
Can you survive?
Can you fight?
Can you be useful?
Can you escape when it comes down to it?
Learning to assess these things was the first step for an adventurer.
In fact, they often taught it before teaching how to use a sword.
The boy with reddish-brown hair was clearly out of place.
He lacked both skill and resolve.
Was he a hand-me-down, a gift, or just some unlucky kid who left his belongings in the field?
The hand holding the worn-out sword was trembling, and his stance was shaky.
Even if the boy were a genius, he wouldn’t be able to fight properly.
Barrel’s prediction quickly came true as the boy was knocked down by a monster’s charge.
As expected, he seemed unable to use body enhancement properly. Why on earth was he here?
Barrel was irritated by the boy. He should just stay out of the way.
There were plenty of other adventurers, and losing one wouldn’t cause a collapse.
More importantly, he was of no use whether he was there or not.
In the world of adventurers, it was a matter of self-responsibility.
And right now, there was no one with the luxury to worry about a young adventurer who had tripped over a monster.
The monster, sensing the huge opening presented by the boy tripping, lunged to finish him off.
What was that?
No, I can’t think straight.
Barrel stared blankly at the humanoid monster with four arms. He couldn’t recall the name of the monster.
But he understood that the monster was “somewhat” dangerous.
If that arm came down, the boy would die.
He might die even if he took it head-on.
This kid was going to die.
Barrel intended to abandon the boy.
To throw himself into danger to save someone was not something a “somewhat” adventurer like him would do.
And right now, there were only “somewhat” adventurers like him present.
They were all adventurers who could only defeat monsters safely in safe places and earn just enough to live a decent life.
So that boy was going to die. It couldn’t be helped. It was his fault for being here without the necessary skills.
As he thought that, his body moved instinctively. He grabbed the boy by the collar and jumped desperately.
The monster’s fist that brushed past him certainly had the power to kill, and he thought he was dead.
What am I doing?
Barrel was angry at himself for having brushed against the edge of death, and he was angry at the boy for making him do so.
This was far from his character.
While forcibly pulling the boy up, he shouted orders to the surrounding adventurers.
There’s something dangerous, so surround it and beat it down.
The adventurers, who had managed to coordinate somewhat while fighting together, began to pummel the unnamed four-armed monster.
He had done something out of character, but he was still alive.
Grateful for that luck, Barrel called out to the boy.
He had been angry, so he intended to tell him to hurry back to town.
“Do you have a master?”
The words that came out were incomprehensible even to himself.
“I just became an adventurer recently and haven’t found a master yet.”
The boy replied in a trembling voice, and what came out next was even more incomprehensible.
“Then I’ll be your master.
Mention my name, Barrel, at the Guild, and I’ll take you on as my disciple.
But right now, you’re in the way, so hurry and retreat to a safe place.”
What on earth am I saying?
For a moment, the boy’s face brightened at his words, but he quickly tightened his expression, realizing it was out of place, and ran off.
As he watched the boy’s back, Barrel was bewildered.
He had thought he wasn’t the kind of person who could take on a disciple. He was aware of that.
He had the skill to use others when necessary, but he wasn’t the kind of person who could teach and guide others.
After all, he hadn’t been in charge during the previous Forest Dragon’s magic stone search, and he wasn’t leading this time either.
The reasons were that the last time it was for money, and this time… what was it this time?
Ignoring the curious gazes from his fellow adventurers, who were thinking, “Hey, what’s up?
That’s pretty cool,” Barrel shouted orders to crush the monster’s head.
Why are you all able to laugh in such a tough situation? Are you idiots?
He was exasperated by the adventurers who were grinning at him. Then he realized.
Ah, damn it. Barrel groaned. I’m laughing too.
Barrel realized what he was fighting for.
What the hell, am I fighting to become a cool adventurer?
He laughed at the absurdity of it all. For some reason, the surrounding fools started laughing too.
Having lost his parents and received no help from anyone, he had become an adventurer because he had no other choice.
Among them, he had seen a few cool adventurers.
Did he want to become one of those cool adventurers he had seen a few times?
It was not very smart.
Barrel was exasperated with himself.
Being satisfied with being “somewhat” means living wisely.
But this was not very wise.
Admiration is something you respect and praise, but it’s not something you try to become.
That was Barrel’s belief.
He admired because he thought he couldn’t become like that.
Like his beloved “bearded Longdagger.”
Barrel lamented that his cleverness was indeed superficial.
It was probably because he had met the real thing.
In their first meeting, he had seen the “beardless Longdagger” roll a monster on the ground with a technique.
Having seen the real thing, he couldn’t help but think that he wanted to be a cool adventurer, to step just a little beyond “somewhat.”
That’s why he felt the urge to show off in front of the novice adventurer. It was not very wise.
His superficial cleverness couldn’t hide the influence of having seen the real deal.
He couldn’t turn a blind eye to it.
The admiration that the sulky kid had held onto.
Ah, damn it, I’m an adventurer, Barrel lamented, having nearly died about thirty times when a sudden explosion erupted from the Demon Realm’s forest.
While desperately trying to calm the confused adventurers, he urged himself, just take that half-step forward, you’re almost there.
Dying would be embarrassing; if he didn’t live, he couldn’t become cool.
His body was covered in wounds, and he was muddy and dirty from rolling around, but that didn’t matter for coolness.
As long as he was alive, he was cool.
And the end came abruptly. The horde of monsters that had spilled out from the forest slowly began to retreat.
“See? It doesn’t matter what you look like.”
Barrel muttered with a dazed expression. He was too exhausted to think straight.
Finally managing to drive back the horde of monsters, he saw Shin and the others emerge from the forest, cutting through the monsters.
Shin, who was leading the way, was battered and bloodied.
“Looks like the ‘beardless Longdagger’ is doing well.”
Barrel burned the image of the cool adventurer he had once admired into his memory.
Comsas Dortwill, the lord of the Makikomaru Claw Barony and a noble standing at the forefront of the Demon Realm in Hekatai, was clinging to his desk in his room, enduring the pain in his stomach.
The fact that healing magic was ineffective meant it was something mental.
He knew the cause.
It was all because of the exiled marquis daughter from Faltarl and her nominal husband.
It was fine that they had defeated the Forest Dragon, which was a designated target for the Adventurer Guild, but they were the kind of people who could take down three Golden Ogres together.
They could probably pull that off.
That was fine; he had a lot to say about how they should have lived a quiet hermit life in Hekatai, but he could still somewhat understand that.
After all, they were adventurers; such things could happen.
However.
What kind of reasoning was it for someone who had been sentenced to death by the Church and exiled to receive a request from the Church in another country?
Not to mention, being asked to retrieve a sacred artifact left behind in the Demon Realm, a secret of the Church, made no sense at all.
Both the one making the request and the one receiving it were insane.
When Vival, the Bishop and the highest authority in the Makikomaru Claw Barony, asked him to cooperate with that former marquis daughter, Comsas almost asked if it was to assist in an assassination.
The Church and the former marquis daughter were both incomprehensible to Comsas.
It transcended the level of being nonsensical; it seemed like they were in a state of madness while remaining sane.
Even dandelion fluff danced more systematically.
On top of that.
Comsas groaned, holding his aching stomach, and looked out the window.
Some fool was setting off fireworks in the town despite it being prohibited, and he could hear the popping sounds.
They’re actually succeeding…
Comsas sighed, aware that his inner voice had become pathetic.
Moreover, according to the hastily compiled report from the Guild, the adventurers were celebrating the former marquis daughter or the Longdagger couple as heroes.
Last night, when he read that, Comsas couldn’t help but slam the report onto the floor.
It was the result of his feelings exploding from not understanding.
Even Comsas, who was not well-versed in central politics, understood.
A noble who had been exiled for losing in courtly intrigue wouldn’t normally try to stand out like this.
Comsas thought it was a matter of common sense, not about being knowledgeable or not.
To someone like Comsas, who was timid and disliked unexpected situations, Shin Longdagger and Erika Solnzali were truly beyond his understanding.
Just imagining such a bomb being in his precious town was terrifying.
But even so, Comsas Dortwill was a practical man.

If the adventurers had put their lives on the line to stop the monsters that had spilled out from the Demon Realm, and if he thought that the Longdagger couple was the one who had put an end to it, then it would be a bad move not to reward them.
No matter how he rewarded an exiled former marquis daughter from another country, it seemed like nothing but a source of trouble, but he couldn’t just ignore it.

For now, he decided to make the town’s alcohol free for two days to coincide with the Church’s announcement of the retrieval of the sacred artifact, with the intention of rewarding the adventurers who had fought in the defense.
He seriously fantasized about the Longdagger couple disappearing somewhere during that time.
He knew that such a wish would never come true, but he thought that at least a fantasy was permissible.
Well, it was unlikely that such a thing would happen.
Comsas sighed.
It was a sigh bigger than he had expected.
What should he do?
He felt like he was about to lose to reality.
What on earth would happen in his town from now on? Would that couple quiet down with this?
Imagining it was endless, and the more he thought, the more dreadful scenarios came to mind.
But well, it was probably overthinking to consider that the town would be attacked by a dragon.
Comsas couldn’t help but let out a wry smile at his overly exaggerated imagination.
Ah, I really wish they would just go back to their homeland.
As he listened to the sound of the fireworks being set off again, Comsas couldn’t help but wish for his own peace.
Bishop Vival Vivality, the highest authority in the Makikomaru Claw Barony, was offering prayers at the Church in Hekatai.
